title: Adjunctions descend through localization with their unit and counit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_1,\mathcal C_2,\mathcal D_1,\mathcal D_2$ be categories, $W_i$ classes of morphisms of $\mathcal C_i$, and $Q_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D_i$ localizations at $W_i$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Let $L:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_2$ and $R:\mathcal C_2\to\mathcal C_1$ be adjoint, $L\dashv R$, with unit $\eta:1\to RL$ and counit $\varepsilon:LR\to1$. Suppose functors $\bar L:\mathcal D_1\to\mathcal D_2$, $\bar R:\mathcal D_2\to\mathcal D_1$ are supplied with natural isomorphisms $p:\bar LQ_1\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_2L$ and $q:\bar RQ_2\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_1R$. Then there is an adjunction $\bar L\dashv\bar R$ whose unit and counit satisfy, for $X\in\mathcal C_1$ and $Y\in\mathcal C_2$,
$$
\bar\eta_{Q_1X}=\bar R(p_X^{-1})\circ q_{LX}^{-1}\circ Q_1(\eta_X),\qquad
\bar\varepsilon_{Q_2Y}=Q_2(\varepsilon_Y)\circ p_{RY}\circ\bar L(q_Y).
$$
In particular these induced maps satisfy both triangle identities on the whole localized categories.
